subject: POC capacity planning — Acme AI (next steps & capacity)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from today's POC discovery (capacity + success criteria)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Jordan and Priya — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we can align on capacity and timelines: 

Summary of ask:
- Run a 3-week POC to validate inference latency and cost at expected peak load for your chat product (90th percentile latency < 250ms for 1-2k qps, 99th < 500ms)
- Validate streaming responses and function/tool calls for our multi-turn flows

Suggested success criteria:
- Latency: 90p < 250ms, 99p < 500ms for generation endpoint under target load
- Throughput: sustained 1k qps with bursts to 2k qps for up to 30s
- Cost: token cost per 1M tokens within 20% of projected baseline (we'll provide estimates)
- Stability: <0.5% error rate (server errors/timeouts) during POC window

Capacity assumptions and ask from Acme:
- Typical request size: ~600 tokens/user/session, average 1.8 utterances/session
- Concurrency target: baseline 1k qps, expected burst to 2k qps during peak events

Proposed Redwood infra for POC:
- Reserved GPUs: 4 x A100-40GB for baseline (dedicated pool)
- Autoscaling policy: scale up additional 4 GPUs when 95th CPU/KV-cache saturation sustained > 60s; scale down after 5 min idle
- Burst policy: short-term burst capacity via shared pool (best-effort) for spikes up to 2k qps; we will pre-warm models and maintain KV cache warmers for test periods

Operational/ownership:
- Redwood POC owner: Marissa Cole (will manage infra config, monitoring, and cost reporting)
- Acme POC owner: Jordan Lee (product) and Priya Singh (infra)

Next steps:
1) Acme confirms success criteria and expected peak concurrency by EOD Friday 8/21
2) Redwood to send SOW + capacity plan (attached) by Monday 8/24
3) Target kickoff: week of 8/31 — 3-week run, with interim check at end of week 1

Attachments: acme_poc_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx (capacity numbers + GPU sizing), POC_SOW_draft_acme.pdf

Thanks — I looped in Rishi and Dylan for any questions on kernel/quantization profiles.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's POC discovery (capacity + success criteria)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Burst profile: our busiest events last ~45-60s, not 30s. We need burst handle for up to 60s when product marketing sends promos.
2) Token assumptions: average request closer to 900 tokens. We'll double-check and confirm by EOD.
3) For success criteria on cost, can you include an estimate that separates compute vs network vs storage? Helpful for my finance partner.

Confirmed owners on our side: Priya will handle infra details and I'll drive product validation. We can confirm the final numbers on Friday.

Also, can you provision a short pre-prod window next week (2-3 hours) so Priya can validate connectivity and VPC peering?

—
Jordan Lee
Head of Product | Acme AI
jordan.lee@acme.ai | +1 212-555-0123
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's POC discovery (capacity + success criteria)

Great notes Jordan — answers inline: 

1) Burst window: 60s is fine. We'll adjust burst policy to allow sustained 60s windows up to 2k qps. We'll also set a safety cap to prevent cost runaway: auto-fallback to a lower-cost model variant if bursts exceed 90s cumulatively in a 10-minute window.

2) Token size: please confirm asap — I sized the attached workbook for 600 tokens; 900 tokens will increase baseline GPU needs by roughly 40% (estimated).

3) Cost breakdown: yes — I'll include compute / network / storage line items in the SOW. Rishi, can you add the per-token compute delta for 600 vs 900 average request?

Pre-prod window: yes, we can provision a 2-3 hour pre-prod next Wed 8/26 between 10-1 PT. Priya, does that work?

I'll update the capacity plan and push a revised SOW Monday. If you confirm token avg and accept the 4 A100 baseline for 600 tokens, we'll lock reserved capacity and get your network team the peering details.

—
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's POC discovery (capacity + success criteria)

Quick compute numbers (high-level) — we'll include detailed table in the SOW: 

- Baseline (600 tokens avg): 4 x A100-40GB reserved -> supports ~1k qps with our current quantized LLM build (approx 20ms/token on average; batching assumed)
- If avg request = 900 tokens: recommended baseline increases to 6 x A100-40GB to maintain 1k qps with same latency profile
- Burst handling (to 2k qps for 60s): pre-warm and use 4 additional on-demand GPUs from shared pool; expect some added latency during scale-up but within 99p target if KV caches pre-warmed

Notes: quantization profile we plan to use is INT8 mixed with selective FP16 for attention kernels; that gives ~1.8x perf uplift vs pure FP16 in our tests. Details in the attached workbook.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Inference Engineering | Redwood Inference
